seoTitle: How to Upgrade Your Hostinger Plan and Balance
metaDescription: Upgrade a Hostinger hosting plan in 2026: how the comparison screen credits unused time from your current plan, why VPS isn't a direct upgrade option, and what changes if your IP address updates.
intro: As a website grows, a basic hosting plan can start to feel limiting. Upgrading on Hostinger doesn't mean losing money already paid: the upgrade screen works out what's left on your current term and knocks it off the new plan's price, so the number you pay is almost never the sticker price. This guide walks through that comparison screen as it appears, current plan against upgrade target, balance credit, and the final amount due, plus one limit worth knowing before you start: this screen moves you between Web and Cloud tiers, not onto a VPS.
prerequisites: An existing Hostinger Web or Cloud hosting plan with an active website on it
costNote: Upgrading costs money unless your existing balance fully covers it. Hostinger converts the unused value of your current term into a discount on the new plan, so the amount due is usually less than the plan's full price, but it is rarely zero.

steps.heading: Open the upgrade comparison for your site
steps.body:
From the Websites section of your Hostinger dashboard, find the upgrade option for the site whose plan you want to change (the same screen is also reachable from Billing > Subscriptions). It opens a two-column comparison: your current plan on the left, the plan you're upgrading to on the right, with a dropdown at the top of the right column for picking the target tier. Each column lists price, visit limits, storage, RAM, CPU cores, PHP workers, and database connections side by side, so you can see what more money buys before committing.

This screen only moves you between Web and Cloud hosting tiers. It does not offer a direct path to a VPS plan or to Agency hosting; those require a separate purchase and a manual (or, for Agency, tool-assisted) migration of your site. Cloud Enterprise also has no upgrade path from here.

image.caption: The upgrade comparison screen. Current plan sits beside the upgrade target, with resource limits lined up row by row and the checkout summary on the right.

steps.heading: Pick the new plan from the dropdown
steps.body: The "Choose hosting plan" dropdown at the top of the right-hand column is where the selection happens. In this walkthrough it's set to Cloud Professional Hosting, one tier above the existing Cloud Startup plan. Changing this dropdown updates every number below it live: price, resource table, and checkout summary all recalculate at once, so it's easy to flip between tiers and compare the real monthly cost of each before settling on one.

image.caption: The plan dropdown set to Cloud Professional Hosting, with the resulting price, resource table, and checkout total updating on the right.

steps.heading: Check the balance credit and billing period together
steps.body:
The checkout panel lists Taxes & Fees, a Total, then a Hostinger balance line shown as a negative amount: the unused, already-paid portion of your current term, credited against the new plan. Below that sits an optional coupon field, then Amount To Pay, the real number charged once the balance and any coupon are subtracted. Hostinger's own example is a $50 remaining balance against a $200 upgrade, leaving $150 due; the walkthrough shown here brought a 12-month upgrade down to under ₹200 because the existing balance covered most of it.

Above that summary, "Choose billing period" switches between terms, commonly 12 or 48 months. Each option changes both the monthly rate and how the balance gets applied, since a longer term spreads the same credit across a bigger total. Toggle between the available periods once before paying: the cheaper-looking monthly rate on a longer plan doesn't always mean a lower amount due today.

image.caption: Choose billing period expanded to show 48-month and 12-month options, sitting directly above the balance-adjusted Amount To Pay.

steps.heading: Confirm, then check the new plan is live
steps.body:
With the plan, billing period, and any coupon set, choosing a payment method finalizes the upgrade. The summary also shows the new expiration date and the rate the plan renews at afterward. Hostinger states upgrades take effect immediately, though moving files, email, and databases to the new plan can take a few hours to finish in the background, so give it a little time before assuming something is wrong.

If you upgraded from Web hosting to a Cloud plan, you'll also get a new dedicated IP address, visible on the Account details page. Update any FTP connections, remote database connections, or DNS A records that pointed at the old IP. Hostinger proxies traffic to the new server for 7 days after the transfer, which is the window to make that DNS change before anything breaks for visitors.

troubleshooting.problem: VPS doesn't appear as an option in the upgrade dropdown
troubleshooting.cause: Web and Cloud hosting plans cannot be upgraded directly to a VPS through this screen.
troubleshooting.fix: Purchase a VPS plan separately from the Billing section, then migrate your site content to it manually.

troubleshooting.problem: The site or mailboxes stop resolving right after upgrading
troubleshooting.cause: Upgrading from Web hosting to a Cloud plan assigns a new dedicated IP address, different from the old Web hosting IP.
troubleshooting.fix: Update FTP connections, remote database connections, and DNS A records to the new IP on the Account details page. Traffic is proxied to the new server for 7 days, so there's a short grace window to make the DNS change.

troubleshooting.problem: The new RAM, CPU, or storage limits don't show up straight after paying
troubleshooting.cause: Hostinger applies the upgrade immediately for billing purposes, but moving files, email, and databases to the new plan can still take a few hours.
troubleshooting.fix: Wait and refresh hPanel before assuming the upgrade failed.

troubleshooting.problem: There's no upgrade button at all on a Cloud Enterprise or Agency plan
troubleshooting.cause: Those two plans don't support upgrades through this screen.
troubleshooting.fix: Agency plans move to a new plan using the Clone Website tool (available only on Agency); Cloud Enterprise has no upgrade path and would mean migrating to a VPS instead.

faq.question: Will I lose the money I've already paid if I upgrade?
faq.answer: No. The checkout screen shows a Hostinger balance line that credits the unused portion of your current term against the new plan's cost, instead of charging you from zero.

faq.question: Can I upgrade straight from shared or Cloud hosting to a VPS?
faq.answer: No. Hostinger's own documentation says Web and Cloud hosting plans can't be upgraded directly to a VPS through this screen; a VPS has to be purchased separately, with the site content migrated over manually.

faq.question: Does upgrading change my site's IP address?
faq.answer: Only when moving from Web hosting to a Cloud plan. Cloud-to-Cloud upgrades, like Cloud Startup to Cloud Professional, keep the existing IP.

faq.question: Does the billing period I choose affect what I pay today?
faq.answer: Yes. Switching between the available billing periods, for example 12 months versus 48, changes both the monthly rate and how the existing balance is applied. Compare both before confirming.

faq.question: Does upgrading cause downtime?
faq.answer: Hostinger describes the upgrade as taking effect immediately, though the underlying file, email, and database transfer can take a few hours to finish.

faq.question: Can Cloud Enterprise or Agency plans upgrade the same way?
faq.answer: No. Both are excluded from this upgrade screen; Agency plans move using the separate Clone Website tool, and Cloud Enterprise has no listed upgrade path.
